newsitem.title: UK: W H Smith says current sales patchy.
newsitem.headline: W H Smith says current sales patchy.

text.p: UK retailer W H Smith Group Plc said on Wednesday that its sales performance in the current year was patchy.
It noted positive sales trends in books, news, magazines and stationery, but sales of music, video and computer games had been disappointing. It blamed fewer quality new releases than last year.
The group said that sales of Olympic merchandise in the U.S. had boosted performance in airport and hotel shops although, as in the UK, music sales were disappointing.

W H Smith, one of the UK's largest newsgents that earlier reported a year pretax loss of 194.7 million stg after charges following a major business review, said it had created a platform for significant performance improvement and increased shareholder value.

"It is early in the recovery process and it will take some time fully to capture all the benefits, but (we are) confident we have made the right decisions to enable managers to achieve greater success," the group said in a statement.

The company levied a 123.0 million stg charge before tax against its results for the strategic review. This included provisions for redundancies, fixed asset and stock write-offs and property and other costs.
The sale of land and buildings during the year also clocked up a loss of nine million stg.
W H Smith's head office has been restructured, 109 jobs were slashed from 398, and it will be moving to smaller premises in London's financial district in September.

"The top business priorities are improved customer services delivered by motivated staff to produce better sales, margins and profitability," said group chief executive Bill Cockburn in the results statement.
The group held its final dividend unchanged at 10.4 pence, maintaining its total dividend at last year's level of 15.65p per share.
